description: A dotted column reference is checked PART BY PART, however many parts it has. Frostlake asked the question only of a SINGLE-part qualifier - the comment said multi-part ones resolve further down - so test_schema.nosuchtable.a found the column by name alone and answered a row. Every part must match: two, three and four parts all read the column when they do, and a wrong COLUMN or a wrong TABLE part is refused at every length with the whole path named in the message. An ALIAS REPLACES the table's name, however many parts precede it, so kw.a and test_schema.kw.a are both invalid once the FROM carries an alias. The qualifier must be a contiguous right-SUFFIX of the relation's full name, so SKIPPING a level (test_db.kw.a, leaving out the schema) is refused as firmly as naming the wrong one. And it is the relation's OWN name that counts, not the schema currently in use: a table in other_schema is qualified by other_schema even while test_schema is current. A keyword after the dots is a name like any other. Converted 1:1 from query/QualifiedReferenceTest (now retired); the Java flattened newlines out of the message before matching, so the converted steps pin the position and the identifier across a REAL newline.
